header.userPrompt:
# Clean up mutually-exclusive / ad-hoc frontend state across the remaining pages

Apply the two frontend state conventions (`.orca/reviewers/frontend.md`) to the
pages an audit found still violating them. Each item below is a **pure,
behaviour-preserving** change — identical UI and behaviour, frontend only, no
API/server/styling changes. (The `BankStatementReview*` components were already
done; do not touch them.)

## A. Model mutually-exclusive state as one ADT

### 1. `ReceiptsPage.scala` — receipt interaction mode
`confirmingId` (L143), `linkingId` (L156), `selectedReceiptId` (L181) are an
exclusive mode — handlers set one and clear the others (e.g. L433-434,
L1503-1505). `confirmRowId` (L162) and the `confirm*` text fields (L144-153) are
the payload of the "confirming" case. Replace with one `useState` of an ADT,
e.g.:
```scala
enum ReceiptMode:
  case Viewing(selected: Option[UUID])
  case Confirming(receiptId: UUID, rowId: Option[UUID])
  case Linking(receiptId: UUID)
```
Opening a mode becomes one assignment; closing returns to `Viewing(None)`.

### 2. `ReceiptsPage.scala` — the two batch machines
`batchProgress` (L133) + `batchResults` (L134), and `batchConfirmProgress`
(L169) + `batchConfirmResults` (L170), are each one `Idle → Running → Done`
machine split across two fields that drift (progress `None` while results
remain). Replace each pair with one ADT (same shape as the `BulkRun` type the
review page now uses — reuse/mirror it):
```scala
enum BatchState:
  case Idle
  case Running(done: Int, total: Int, failed: Int)
  case Done(results: List[(String, Either[String, Unit])])
```

### 3. `UserEditPage.scala` — Telegram link and MCP token actions
Two independent button-triggered async actions, each split across three fields:
Telegram (`telegramToken` L30, `telegramError` L31, `telegramWorking` L32) and
MCP (`mcpToken` L33, `mcpError` L34, `mcpWorking` L35). Each is one machine;
the start handler sets `working=true` and clears token+error together
(L52-54, L71-73). Replace each with one ADT held in one `useState`:
```scala
enum <Thing>State:
  case Idle
  case Working
  case Loaded(token: <TokenType>)
  case Failed(message: String)
```
(These are actions, not page loads, so `AsyncComponent` does not apply — an ADT
is the right model.)

## B. Convert ad-hoc page-load fetches to AsyncComponent

These pages fetch their initial data in a `useEffect` with a `loading` +
`data` + `error` triple instead of `AsyncComponent` — the first rule in
`.orca/reviewers/frontend.md`. Convert each so the fetch goes through
`AsyncComponent` (which renders loading/error and hands the content its data),
removing the manual triple. Model it exactly like the other pages/widgets that
already use `AsyncComponent` (e.g. `ExpensesPage`, `ChartsPage`,
`BankStatementAutoReconcilePage`).

- `BankStatementTemplatePage.scala` — `loading` (L50) + `payloadOpt` (L51) +
  `error` (L54).
- `BulkExpenseCreationPage.scala` — `loading` (L49) + `error` (L50) + data
  (`allRows`/`merchants`/`categories`, L51-53).
- `BulkMerchantSetupPage.scala` — `loading` (L63) + `error` (L64) + data
  (`allRows`/`ruleList`/`merchants`/`categories`, L65-68).

Where such a page also has a small save-action pair (`saving`/`saveError`,
`busy`, etc.), model that as a tiny `Idle/Saving/Failed` ADT too — but a lone
flag with no excluded sibling may stay as-is.

## Constraints

- Behaviour-preserving: identical UI, flows, messages, counts, toasts, and data
  flow. No API/server/styling changes.
- Follow `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md` (both rules) and the project's frontend
  conventions (`FunctionalComponent`/`Props`; object-level `val`s hold only
  plain JS literals; `def` for reused React elements; MUI callbacks read Scala
  via `(opt: Any) match`; new views stay reachable). For the AsyncComponent
  conversions, split the fetched content into a child component that takes the
  loaded data as props, as the existing pages do.
- Line numbers above are from the audit and may have shifted slightly — locate
  the state by name.
- Tests stay green and move/extend with the code; `web/Test/compile` passes.

## Out of scope

- No change to what any of these features do, to server code, or to pages the
  audit cleared (ExpensesPage, RefundsPage, MerchantsPage, ImportRulesPage,
  SavingsPage, CategoriesPage, Charts/Reports, auth widgets).
- The already-refactored `BankStatementReview*` / `BankStatementBulkRuns` /
  `BankStatementReviewLogic` — leave them.

## Acceptance

- `ReceiptsPage` holds one `ReceiptMode` and one `BatchState` per batch op
  instead of the parallel `Option`/progress flags; `UserEditPage` holds one
  state per async action; the three bulk/template pages fetch via
  `AsyncComponent` with no manual loading/data/error triple.
- No handler resets a group of sibling `useState`s any more.
- Every page behaves exactly as before; `web/Test/compile` passes and all web
  tests pass.

resultJson.description:
Bring the remaining frontend pages in line with the two rules in `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md`. Rule 1: page-load data goes through `AsyncComponent`, with no hand-written loading/data/error triple. Rule 2: mutually-exclusive UI state is one ADT held in one `useState`, not several sibling flags that every handler has to reset together. The audit found violations in five pages. `ReceiptsPage` (`ReceiptList`) has the receipt interaction mode plus two batch machines. `UserEditPage` has two token actions. `BankStatementTemplatePage`, `BulkExpenseCreationPage` and `BulkMerchantSetupPage` each load their data with an ad-hoc `useEffect` plus `loading`/`error` flags, and some also have a small save-action flag pair.

Every change must be a pure refactor that preserves behaviour: same UI, flows, labels, counts, toasts and API calls, frontend only, with no server/API/styling changes. The point is that illegal combinations can no longer be represented (two modes open at once, progress set but results missing, `working=true` alongside a stale token). Each transition becomes one assignment, and no handler resets a group of sibling `useState`s. The pure parts of each ADT (transition and derived-value methods) get plain ScalaTest unit tests, following the `BulkRun`/`DrawerState` tests in `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec`.

Out of scope: the already-refactored `BankStatementReview*`, `BankStatementBulkRuns` and `BankStatementReviewLogic` (read them as the model but don't edit them), the pages the audit cleared, and server code. A few remaining ad-hoc fetches that the audit did not list also stay as they are: `UserEditPage`'s `getEnvironmentConfig` effect, and `ReceiptList`'s on-mount `getExpenses`/`getImportRules` effect and on-demand `getAllBankStatementRows`/`getExpenses` calls.

tasks.title: UserEditPage: model Telegram-link and MCP-token actions as one ADT each
tasks.description:
In `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/UserEditPage.scala`, replace the triples `telegramToken`/`telegramError`/`telegramWorking` and `mcpToken`/`mcpError`/`mcpWorking` with one `useState` each, holding a token-action ADT.

Recommended: one generic enum in the `UserEditPage` object, used for both actions:

```scala
enum TokenAction[+T] {
  case Idle
  case Working
  case Loaded(token: T)
  case Failed(message: String)
}
```

It is used as `TokenAction[TelegramLinkToken]` and `TokenAction[McpApiToken]`, with small helpers such as `isWorking: Boolean`, `tokenOpt: Option[T]` and `errorOpt: Option[String]`, so the render code stays a near 1:1 mapping. In Scala 3, a non-parameterised case of a covariant enum extends `TokenAction[Nothing]`.

Transitions:
- `handleX` sets `Working` (one assignment, replacing the three resets).
- Success sets `Loaded(res.token)` and failure sets `Failed(ex.getMessage)`. Both stay guarded by `mounted.current`, exactly as now.

Render must stay identical:
- The primary button and "Regenerate" are disabled while `Working`.
- `CircularLoader` shows while `Working`.
- The token block (including the Telegram bot link from `envConfig`) shows only for `Loaded`.
- `ErrorLabel` shows only for `Failed`.

Today a token disappears when regeneration starts and errors are cleared on start; the ADT reproduces both automatically.

Leave the `envConfig` effect, the `mounted` ref and the tabs unchanged.

Tests: add `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/UserEditPageSpec.scala` (AnyWordSpec, must-matchers, `should` subjects without the object name), covering the helper methods for each case.

Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *UserEditPageSpec"`.

tasks.title: ReceiptsPage: replace the two batch progress/results pairs with a BatchState ADT
tasks.description:
In `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/ReceiptsPage.scala` (component `ReceiptList`), replace `batchProgress`+`batchResults` (upload) and `batchConfirmProgress`+`batchConfirmResults` (batch confirm) with one `useState[BatchState]` each.

**Defining the type.** Mirror `BankStatementReviewLogic.BulkRun` (don't edit that file). Put the enum somewhere testable, for example a new pure object `ReceiptsLogic` in `pages/ReceiptsLogic.scala`, or inside the `ReceiptList` object. Results are `List[(String, Either[String, Unit])]` (label → outcome). Results must stay visible while running, because the upload results list and its Clear button render during a run today. So `Running` carries the results, not just counts. Recommended shape:

```scala
enum BatchState {
  case Idle
  case Running(done: Int, total: Int, failed: Int, results: Results)
  case Done(results: Results)
}
```

Add helper methods:
- `results: Results` (Nil for Idle)
- `isRunning: Boolean`
- `recorded(label, outcome)`: Running only. Increments `done`, increments `failed` when the outcome is Left, and appends the result.
- `finished`: Running → Done(results), otherwise unchanged.
- `cleared`: Done → Idle; Running → `copy(results = Nil)`, which keeps the counters exactly as today's "Clear" mid-run does.

Keeping explicit `done`/`failed` counters (rather than deriving them from `results`) is what keeps Clear-during-a-run behaving identically.

**Wiring.**
- `handleFilesBatch`: start = `Running(0, total, 0, Nil)` (one assignment). Each per-file outcome becomes `setBatch(_.recorded(name, outcome))`, keeping the same labels and messages ("Already uploaded (duplicate)", "File read error", `ex.getMessage`). The end of the loop becomes `setBatch(_.finished)`. The local `done`/`failed` loop counters can go.
- `handleBatchConfirm`: the same pattern. On finish, still clear `batchConfirmSelectedIds`.
- `clearBatchResultsButton`: `setBatch(_.cleared)`.
- `batchActiveKey` and the drag/drop effect: use `batch.isRunning` where `batchProgress.isDefined` was used.
- Render: show the "Uploading: d/t (f failed)…" / "Confirming: …" text when Running, otherwise the previous `None` branch. Render the results lists from `.results` when non-empty. This applies to both the batch-mode header and the left-panel upload controls.

**Batch-confirm subtlety.** `enterBatchConfirmMode` and the Back button currently call `setBatchConfirmProgress(None)` and never clear results. Results from a previous batch confirm therefore persist across re-entry, so don't reset them. When the state is Idle or Done this reset was a no-op. Recommended: drop the reset and leave the batch-confirm state untouched on enter/Back. The only difference is that a run abandoned mid-flight via Back keeps showing its progress if you re-enter, which the old code also did as soon as the next result arrived. Note this in a short comment.

Tests: a pure spec, e.g. `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/ReceiptsLogicSpec.scala`, covering `recorded` (counts and failures, no-op when not running), `finished`, `cleared` (including mid-run) and `isRunning`.

Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and targeted `testOnly`.

tasks.title: ReceiptsPage: model receipt selection/confirm/link as one ReceiptMode ADT
tasks.description:
In `ReceiptList` (`ReceiptsPage.scala`), replace these with one `useState[ReceiptMode]`:
- `selectedReceiptId`, `confirmingId`, `linkingId`
- the confirm-form payload: `confirmAmount`, `confirmDate`, `confirmTime`, `confirmMerchantId`, `confirmMerchantInput`, `confirmNotes`, `confirmSplits`, `confirmParsedMerchantName`, `confirmRowId`

Recommended shape, in the same testable place as the BatchState type if one exists, otherwise the `ReceiptList` object or a `ReceiptsLogic` object:

```scala
final case class ConfirmForm(amount: String, date: String, time: String, merchantId: String, merchantInput: String,
  notes: String, splits: List[(String, String, String)], parsedMerchantName: Option[String], rowId: Option[UUID])

enum ReceiptMode {
  case Viewing(selected: Option[UUID])
  case Confirming(receiptId: UUID, form: ConfirmForm)
  case Linking(receiptId: UUID)
  def selectedId: Option[UUID] = ...  // Viewing(s) => s; Confirming/Linking => Some(receiptId)
}
```

Editing the form: add a helper inside the component, `def updateForm(f: ConfirmForm => ConfirmForm): Unit = setMode { case c: ReceiptMode.Confirming => c.copy(form = f(c.form)); case other => other }`. Always use functional updates, because the Autocomplete `onChange` and `onInputChange` handlers fire back-to-back. `splitsSection` and `splitRow` take `setSplits: List[...] => Unit`, so pass `s => updateForm(_.copy(splits = s))`.

Transitions, mapped from today's code:
- Clicking a list row: `Viewing(Some(r.id))`. This replaces the three sets at the row `onClick`.
- Confirm button: `Confirming(r.id, form)`. Build `form` in one go from `r` (amount, date, `parsedMerchantName`, `rowId = None`, splits `Nil`) plus the tax-id / `ImportRuleMatcher.findReceiptWinner(effectiveRuleList, …)` merchant resolution. Keep the `getAllBankStatementRows` → `setRowList` fetch unchanged.
- Form Cancel: `Viewing(Some(r.id))`.
- `handleConfirm` success: return to `Viewing(Some(receiptId))`, but only if the state is still `Confirming` for that id. Keep the toast, `setError("")` and the receipt refresh.
- `openLinkMode`: `Linking(receiptId)`. `expenseFilter` and `expenseList` stay as separate state, since they are fetched data and a filter, not the mode.
- Link Cancel and link success: `Viewing(Some(receiptId))`.
- The auto-select effect: when `mode.selectedId` is not among the visible receipts, set `Viewing(visibleForFilter.headOption.map(_.id))`.
- The preview effect, `selectedIdKey`, row highlighting and the right panel: use `mode.selectedId`.
- `renderReceiptDetail`: derive `isConfirming`/`isLinking` (and the form) by matching the mode against `r.id`.
- `handleConfirm`: reads its fields from the `Confirming` form.

Behaviour note for the implementer:
- Old code only overwrote `confirmAmount`/`confirmDate`/merchant fields when the receipt had values, and Cancel didn't clear them, so stale values could leak into the next receipt's form. Starting each `Confirming` from a fresh form (""/Nil/None, then filled from `r`) is the intended semantics of the ADT and matches the post-success state.
- A stale `confirmingId` for a receipt that is no longer shown is now dropped. Call both out in the commit message as unrepresentable-state cleanups, not feature changes.

Unrelated state stays: `error`, `toast`, `pollingIds`, `previewUrl`/`previewLoading`, `rowList`, `batchConfirmMode`, `resolvedMerchantIds`, `batchConfirmSelectedIds`, `showIgnored`, `receiptFilter`/`receiptPage`.

Tests: extend the receipts logic spec with `ReceiptMode.selectedId` for each case, plus any pure form-building helper you extract (e.g. building the initial `ConfirmForm` from a receipt plus merchants plus rules). Testing that helper is recommended.

Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and targeted `testOnly`.

tasks.title: BankStatementTemplatePage: load via AsyncComponent and model busy/error as SaveState
tasks.description:
Convert `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementTemplatePage.scala`.

**Outer component (`BankStatementTemplatePage.component`).** Keep the title box and `draftIdOpt` parsing.
- `None` must render the same as today: the "This draft isn't ready yet, or no longer exists." text plus the red "Invalid draft" line below it.
- `Some(id)`: render `AsyncComponent[(BankStatementDraft.Data, List[String])]` with:
  - `fetch = () => for { draft <- client.getBankStatementDraft(id); stmts <- client.getBankStatements } yield (draft, stmts.data.map(_.bankName).distinct.sorted)` (the same sequential fetch as today)
  - `progressIndicator = () => Loader(props.ctx)`
  - `watchedObjects = List(id)` (the old effect re-ran on draftId change)
  - `render` to a new child component, e.g. `object BankStatementTemplateEditor` in the same file, following RULE-FE-001 (`apply` returns `KeyAddingStage`, `case class Props(ctx, draftId: UUID, draft: BankStatementDraft.Data, bankNames: List[String])`), keyed with `.withKey(id.toString)` so its state resets per draft.

**Child component.**
- Holds `payloadOpt` as `useState(props.draft.payload)`. `filename` and `bankNames` become plain props.
- Contains `setMeta`/`setTxn`/`removeTxn`, `doSave`/`doConfirm`/`doDiscard`, the field helpers and `editingView`.
- Calls `useHistory()` itself.

Replace `busy`+`error` with one `useState[SaveState]`. Create a new shared ADT at `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/models/SaveState.scala`, intended for reuse by the other bulk pages:

```scala
enum SaveState {
  case Idle
  case Saving
  case Failed(message: String)
  def isSaving: Boolean = ...
  def errorOpt: Option[String] = ...
}
```

Action transitions:
- Start: `Saving`.
- Failure: `Failed(ex.getMessage)`.
- Save success: `Idle` (still applying the returned payload).
- Confirm/discard success: navigate exactly as today and leave the state `Saving`, just as `busy` stayed true.
- The `"Saving…"`/"Save changes" label, every `.disabled(busy)` and `canConfirm` use `isSaving`.
- The red error line below the content renders `errorOpt`, keeping the same style and position.

Load errors are now rendered by `AsyncComponent`, and the loading view is `Loader` instead of the inline "Loading…". This presentation change is accepted by the epic.

Keep `amountColor`/`metaComplete` on `BankStatementTemplatePage` (the existing spec calls them there).

Tests: add `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/models/SaveStateSpec.scala` covering `isSaving` and `errorOpt` per case. Keep `BankStatementTemplatePageSpec` green.

Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *SaveStateSpec *BankStatementTemplatePageSpec"`.

tasks.title: BulkExpenseCreationPage: load via AsyncComponent and use SaveState for import/ignore
tasks.description:
Convert `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BulkExpenseCreationPage.scala`. This builds on the `net.wiringbits.models.SaveState` ADT from the template-page task.

**Outer component.** Render `AsyncComponent[(GetAllRows.Response, GetMerchants.Response, GetCategories.Response)]`:
- `fetch`: the same sequential for-comprehension as today (`getAllBankStatementRows`, `getMerchants`, `getCategories`).
- `progressIndicator = () => Loader(props.ctx)`.
- No `watchedObjects`: the old effect ran once, and desc changes must not refetch.
- `render` to a new child component in the same file, e.g. `object BulkExpenseCreationContent` (RULE-FE-001; Props: `ctx`, `rows: List[GetAllRows.RowData]`, `merchants`, `categories`).

**Child component.**
- Holds `allRows` as `useState(props.rows)`; `allRows` is mutated after import/ignore. `merchants` and `categories` were never mutated after load, so they become plain props.
- Moves `useHistory`, `useTypedLocation`, `descParam`, Screen 1 and Screen 2 state, `resolveCatId`/`resolveMerchantId`, `handleImport`/`handleIgnore`, the Autocomplete setup and both screens' render.
- The "reset Screen 2" effect drops the `loading` dependency, so its deps become `List(descParam.getOrElse(""))`. It runs on child mount, which is equivalent to the old "load completed" run.

Replace `saving`+`saveError` with one `useState[SaveState]`:
- "No rows selected": `Failed("No rows selected")`.
- Start: `Saving`.
- Success: `Idle`.
- Failure: `Failed(ex.getMessage)`.
- The reset effect previously only cleared `saveError`. Use `setSave { case SaveState.Failed(_) => SaveState.Idle; case s => s }` so an in-flight save is not disturbed.
- Disabled flags and the "Processing…" label use `isSaving`. The error Typography renders `errorOpt`.

Remove the `loading`/`error` state and the manual spinner/error branches; `AsyncComponent` handles both. Keep the `private val`s (`PageSize`, `normalize`, `renderTextField`) as they are.

Tests: there is no existing spec for this page. Per RULE-TE-010, don't add a DOM test. If you extract a pure helper while moving code (e.g. the initial-selection computation from the reset effect), unit-test it in `BulkExpenseCreationPageSpec`; otherwise compile plus the SaveState spec is enough.

Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile`.

tasks.title: BulkMerchantSetupPage: load via AsyncComponent and use SaveState in DescriptionRow
tasks.description:
Convert `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BulkMerchantSetupPage.scala`. This builds on `net.wiringbits.models.SaveState`.

**Outer component.** Render `AsyncComponent[(GetAllRows.Response, GetImportRules.Response, GetMerchants.Response, GetCategories.Response)]`:
- `fetch`: the old code creates all four futures before the for-comprehension, so the requests run concurrently. Keep that: `val fRows = …; val fRules = …; …; for {…} yield (…)` inside the fetch lambda.
- `progressIndicator = () => Loader(props.ctx)`.
- No `watchedObjects`.
- `render` to a new child component, e.g. `object BulkMerchantSetupContent` (RULE-FE-001; Props: `ctx`, `rows`, `rules: List[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule]` mapped with `Rule.fromApi`, `merchants`, `categories`).

**Child component.**
- Holds `ruleList`, `merchants` and `categories` as `useState` seeded from props, because `DescriptionRow.onDone` appends to them. `allRows` is never mutated and becomes a plain prop.
- Keeps `useHistory`, `useTypedLocation`, `initialPage`, `page`, `pageChanging` (a lone flag, which stays), the page-change effect, `gotoPage`, the unmatched-groups computation and the render.
- The `loading || pageChanging` spinner branch becomes just `pageChanging`, keeping the same `CircularProgress` box. Remove the manual error branch.

`DescriptionRow` (same file): replace `saving`+`rowError` with one `useState[SaveState]`:
- The validation messages "Merchant name is required" and "Category is required": `Failed(msg)`.
- Start: `Saving`.
- Success: `Idle`.
- Failure: `Failed(ex.getMessage)`.
- Every disabled/label/error-display use maps to `isSaving`/`errorOpt`.

Look at the rest of `DescriptionRow` (below line ~379) for every use of `saving`/`rowError`.

Keep the `findUnmatchedGroups`, `merchantOptionLabel`, `categoryOptionLabel` and `resolveOrCreateCategory` signatures and locations unchanged, because `BulkMerchantSetupPageSpec` and other pages (`ReceiptsPage`, `BulkExpenseCreationPage`) call them.

Tests: keep `BulkMerchantSetupPageSpec` green, including its DescriptionRow render tests. They construct `DescriptionRow.Props` directly, so don't change Props.

Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *BulkMerchantSetupPageSpec"`.

resultJson.brief:
**Modules and directories**
- `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/`: one object per page. Page = `object X { def apply(ctx, user): KeyAddingStage; case class Props; val component: FunctionalComponent[Props] }`. Child components for loaded content live in the same file as extra top-level objects. Examples: `ReceiptsPage` → `ReceiptList`; `BankStatementAutoReconcilePage` → `ReconcileContent`; `BulkMerchantSetupPage.scala` also holds `DescriptionRow`.
- `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/models/`: small UI models (`User`, `UserMenuOption`, `AuthState`). A good home for a shared ADT.
- `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/...`: ScalaTest `AnyWordSpec` + `org.scalatest.matchers.must.Matchers.*`. Test files mirror source paths. `should` subjects must NOT repeat the object/class name (RULE-TE-001). Prefer pure-function/ADT unit tests over DOM tests (RULE-TE-010).
- Routes in `AppRouter.scala` are unaffected; no new pages are added.

**Rules being applied** (`.orca/reviewers/frontend.md`)
1. Fetch API data through `AsyncComponent`, not useEffect plus loading/error flags.
2. Mutually-exclusive `useState`s become one enum held in one `useState`. A lone flag with no excluded sibling (e.g. `pageChanging`, `batchConfirmMode`) may stay.

**AsyncComponent** (library `net.wiringbits %%% slinky-utils`, import `net.wiringbits.webapp.utils.slinkyUtils.components.core.AsyncComponent`; source not in repo)
```scala
AsyncComponent[T](fetch = () => Future[T], render = (t: T) => ReactElement,
  progressIndicator = () => Loader(props.ctx), watchedObjects = List(...))  // watchedObjects optional; refetch on change
```
- It renders loading and errors itself; don't re-implement them.
- `Loader` is `net.wiringbits.components.widgets.Loader`.
- `GenericHooks.useForceRefresh` (`net.wiringbits.webapp.utils.slinkyUtils.core.GenericHooks`) is used for refresh, but none of the pages in this epic refresh.
- `T` can be a tuple. Use one combined Future to keep request ordering/concurrency identical. Existing pages nest AsyncComponents; either compiles.
- Reference implementations: `ReceiptsPage.component` (3 nested), `BankStatementAutoReconcilePage` (invalid-param branch + nested + `ReconcileContent` child), `ChartsPage`, `ExpensesPage`.
- The child receives loaded data as Props. Any data the page later mutates becomes `Hooks.useState(props.x)` in the child.

**ADT precedent to mirror (don't edit)**
`BankStatementReviewLogic.scala` ~L209-260:
- `enum BulkRun { case Idle; case Running(total, results); case Done(results); def results; def isRunning; def recorded(id, outcome); def finished }` plus `object BulkRun { extension (r: Running) { def done; def failed } }`.
- `enum DrawerState { Closed | CreateExpense(rowId) | ... ; def openRowId }`.

Tests are in `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec` ("BulkRun" should …, ~L725). Usage pattern: `Hooks.useState[BulkRun](BulkRun.Idle)`, transitions via functional updates `setX(_.recorded(...))` / `setX(_.finished)` (see `BankStatementBulkRuns.scala`). Use functional updates inside async callbacks and loops: closures capture stale render values.

**Slinky/Scala gotchas**
- `Hooks.useState[T](init)` returns `(value, SetStateHookCallback[T])`. The setter accepts either a value or a `T => T`.
- Scala 3 `enum` with a covariant type param: parameterless cases become `X[Nothing]`.
- Pattern-match on enum cases as `case c: Mode.Confirming =>` or `case Mode.Confirming(id, f) =>`.
- `-Werror` under `CI=true`: unused imports and non-exhaustive matches fail the build. Remove imports your change orphans (e.g. `Hooks`/`Success`/`Failure`/`js`).
- Object-level `val`s may only hold plain JS literals / `CSSPropertiesUtils`, never a `ReactElement`/`KeyAddingStage`. Use `def` for elements reused in one render.
- Keep `.withKey` on mapped lists.
- MUI Autocomplete callbacks use `(value: Any) match { case m: Merchant => ... }`. Keep `DescriptionRow.merchantOptionLabel`/`categoryOptionLabel` (`private[pages]`, also used by `ReceiptsPage` and `BulkExpenseCreationPage`).
- `useHistory()` and `RouterCompat.useTypedLocation()` can be called in child components; they are inside the router.
- Existing `js.Array(...)` effect deps exist in these files. Don't churn unrelated ones. For effects you rewrite, the guide prefers `""` / `List(...)` deps (RULE-FE-006).

**Per-file facts**
- `UserEditPage.scala`:
  - Tokens are `net.wiringbits.common.models.{TelegramLinkToken, McpApiToken}` (`.value`).
  - `client.createTelegramLinkToken` / `createMcpToken` return `Future[...Response]` with `.token`.
  - Results are applied only if `mounted.current`.
  - `envConfig` is a separate fetch; leave it.
- `ReceiptsPage.scala` (~1580 lines). All state is in `ReceiptList.component`:
  - Batch state ~L132-134 and ~L164-170.
  - Mode/form state ~L142-162 and L181.
  - Handlers: `handleFilesBatch` ~L321, `handleConfirm` ~L388, `openLinkMode` ~L432, `handleLinkToExpense` ~L442, `enterBatchConfirmMode` ~L496, `handleBatchConfirm` ~L517, `renderLinkPicker` ~L575 (Cancel sets `linkingId` None), `merchantAutocomplete` ~L621 (writes `confirmMerchantId`/`Input`), `splitsSection`/`splitRow` ~L646-736.
  - Drag/drop effect is keyed on `batchActiveKey` (~L738).
  - Two render sites for upload progress/results: the batch-mode `header` (~L768-895) and the left panel (~L1370-1410).
  - Confirm form render is in `renderReceiptDetail` (~L947-1066); the Confirm button handler is ~L1092-1122.
  - List row click is ~L1502 (sets selected, clears confirming/linking).
  - The right panel uses `selectedReceiptId` (~L1565).
  - Upload batch results are labelled by file name. Batch-confirm results are labelled by `documentFilename` (or the id prefix + "Receipt not found"). `failed` increments exactly when the outcome is Left.
- `BankStatementTemplatePage.scala`:
  - `client.getBankStatementDraft(id): Future[BankStatementDraft.Data]`, where `Data(id, filename, status, error, payload: Option[Payload])`. `client.getBankStatements` returns `.data` with `bankName`.
  - Update/confirm/discard calls are unchanged.
  - The public `amountColor` and `metaComplete` are tested by `BankStatementTemplatePageSpec`; keep them on the object.
- `BulkExpenseCreationPage.scala`:
  - Merchants/categories are never mutated after load; `allRows` is (import/ignore mark rows).
  - The `descParam` reset effect depends on `loading`.
- `BulkMerchantSetupPage.scala`:
  - Four futures fire concurrently.
  - `onDone` appends to rules/merchants/categories.
  - `findUnmatchedGroups` is `private[pages]` and tested.
  - `DescriptionRow.Props` is constructed directly in `BulkMerchantSetupPageSpec`; don't change it.
- `ApiClient` lives at `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/ApiClient.scala`; it is read-only for this epic.

**Build and verify** (no shell restrictions for implementers)
- `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile`, then `sbt "web/testOnly *SpecName"` for the specs touched. Don't run the full `sbt test`.
- Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default shell node is v16, which makes yarn install fail).
